name: G-Shock DW-5000C
case_material: Resin over a floating module, stainless steel screw-back
summary: The first G-Shock, launched in April 1983. Kikuo Ibe's brief was a single line: "a durable watch that would not break even if dropped". The module floats inside a hollow, shock-absorbing resin case. Sources disagree on its original depth rating (100 m or 200 m), so it is not stated here.

name: G-Shock DW-5200C
summary: A near-identical successor to the DW-5000C, released in 1984, the year a US television advert that used the watch as a hockey puck helped turn G-Shock into a hit.

name: G-Shock DW-5500C
summary: Casio's first Mud Resist G-Shock, using two-tone moulding to seal the square case against mud and dust: the ancestor of the later Mudman line.

name: G-Shock DW-5600C
summary: The first "5600", the shape that became the definitive square G-Shock. It sold for nine years until the EL-backlit DW-5600E replaced it in 1996; the module changed from 691 to 901 around 1989 or 1990, depending on the source.

name: G-Shock GW-M5610
complications: alarm; stopwatch; countdown timer; backlight; Tough Solar; Multi-Band 6 radio sync; world time
summary: The square that never needs setting or a battery change: solar-charged and synchronised by radio with atomic clocks. Its GW-M5600 predecessor launched in 2008; the exact debut year of the 5610 is not confirmed by the sources, so it is not stated here.

name: G-Shock GW-5000
complications: alarm; stopwatch; countdown timer; backlight; Tough Solar; Multi-Band 6 radio sync; world time
case_material: Resin with stainless steel case and screw-back (DLC)
summary: A made-in-Japan homage to the 1983 original, with a screw-lock back, solar power and radio sync. It is held in the Victoria and Albert Museum's collection as a 2009 design, and was succeeded by the GW-5000U.

name: G-Shock GW-5000U
complications: alarm; stopwatch; countdown timer; backlight; Tough Solar; Multi-Band 6 radio sync; world time
case_material: Resin with stainless steel case and screw-back (DLC)
summary: The updated, made-in-Japan GW-5000: the new module 3495 adds a full auto LED backlight with adjustable afterglow and an adjustable date format, while keeping the screw-back, solar charging and Multi-Band 6.

name: G-Shock GMW-B5000D "Full Metal"
complications: alarm; stopwatch; countdown timer; backlight; Tough Solar; Multi-Band 6 radio sync; world time; Bluetooth sync
summary: The first full-metal 5000-series G-Shock, released in Japan in April 2018 for the 35th anniversary: the 1983 shape rebuilt in steel with resin shock absorbers between case and bezel, solar power, radio sync and Bluetooth.

name: G-Shock GW-B5600
complications: alarm; stopwatch; countdown timer; backlight; Tough Solar; Multi-Band 6 radio sync; world time; Bluetooth sync
summary: The resin twin of the full-metal GMW-B5000: the same solar, Multi-Band 6 and Bluetooth functions in the classic lightweight 5600 case, announced in Japan in October 2018.

name: G-Shock DW-5040PG "Recrystallized"
case_material: Resin; recrystallised, deep-layer-hardened stainless steel back, buckle and loop
summary: A 40th-anniversary limited edition from the Recrystallized series (2023): the original DW-5000 design, with a case back, buckle and loop in steel treated by recrystallisation and deep-layer hardening.

name: G-Shock DW-5000R "Origin Revival"
case_material: Bio-based resin bezel over stainless steel case, screw-lock back
summary: A standard-issue (non-limited) re-creation of the 1983 DW-5000C, made at Yamagata Casio in Japan, with the screw-lock steel case of the original and a bio-based resin band and bezel.
